title: Quiet at Eleven
sub: PreK–Kindergarten · Poppies, a clock and a quiet time
objective: Children will hear that, long ago, a very big war ended at 11 o’clock in the morning, and that everything went quiet. They will learn that people wear a red poppy to remember the soldiers, and that every year many people keep a quiet time at 11 o’clock. They will count to eleven, find 11 on a clock, and keep a short quiet time of their own.

objectives.heading: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
objectives.why: Long ago a very big war ended at 11 o’clock. Every year since, people have stopped and kept quiet at that time, to remember.

materials: A clock, or the clock on the *Show your class* page (page 3)
A bell, or something that rings
The *Show your class* page, projected or printed
Red crayons, and the differentiated handouts
A paper poppy for each child (optional)
questions: What time did the war stop? Can you find 11 on the clock?
What did people hear when the war was over?
What color is the poppy? Why do people wear one?
Who would you like to say thank you to?
connection: **Visit the exhibition:** look for the red poppies climbing the edge of the *When the Guns Fell Silent* poster, and the date and time in red: **11.11.1918, 11:00**.
**Virtual visit:** in *The Memorial*, place one poppy in the field together. Each poppy there is placed by a visitor to the Mini Museum.

steps.title: Loud, then quiet
script: Sit in a circle. *“Let’s be loud! Clap and stamp, as loud as you can.”* After a few seconds, hold up the clock and stop, very still. Wait for the room to go quiet. Ask: *“How did that feel, when the noise stopped all at once?”* Then: *“A long time ago, something very loud stopped all at once, just like that. Let me tell you about it.”*
steps.purpose: Feel how sudden a silence is, before hearing the story of one.
students: Clap and stamp, as loud as you can!
When the clock goes up, stop. Shh.

steps.title: The day it went quiet
script: Long ago, more than a hundred years ago, there was a very big war. It was loud, and it went on for a long, long time. Then one morning, on the eleventh day of the eleventh month, at **11 o’clock**, it stopped. Everything went quiet. Church bells rang. Some soldiers shook hands. Some cried. The war was over. Hold up the clock: *“Look, here is 11. Let’s count to 11 together on our fingers.”*
steps.purpose: Hear the story: a very big war, and the morning it stopped.
students: What time did it stop? Show me 11 on your fingers.

steps.title: Church bells rang
script: Ring the bell, or play the bells from the exhibition. *“The bells rang because the war was over. People were happy it had stopped. They were sad, too, because some soldiers did not come home.”*
steps.purpose: Hear the bells that rang when the war was over.
students: Were people happy, or sad, or both?

steps.title: A red poppy
script: Red poppies grew in the fields where the soldiers had been. So now, every November, people wear a red poppy. It says: *we remember.* We remember the soldiers who did not come home, and we say thank you to everyone who served. Show the poppies on page 3. *“What color are they? Let’s count them together.”*

steps.title: Your handout
script: Each child works on a handout. All three have the clock, the number 11 and a red poppy.

levels.name: Green Level
levels.summary: Picture-led. Color a big poppy red, circle the clock that says 11 o’clock, color eleven numbered poppies, trace *11*.

levels.name: Yellow Level
levels.summary: A little more. Circle the 11 o’clock clock, count out eleven poppies from a row of twelve, copy *11* under a model, draw a poppy field.

levels.name: Red Level
levels.summary: Draw and tell. Draw the hands at 11 o’clock, color a poppy and tell a grown-up why we wear one, draw someone to thank, finish *Thank you…*

steps.purpose: Count, find 11 and color a poppy, at the right level for each child.

steps.title: Look back
script: Put the questions on the screen. For each one, children show a thumb up, sideways or down: *“Can you now count to eleven, and find 11 on the clock? Can you now say why people wear a red poppy? Can you now keep a quiet time to remember?”*

steps.title: Our quiet time
script: Every year, on November 11 at 11 o’clock, many people stop what they are doing and are quiet for two minutes, to remember. In America we call it Veterans Day. *“Let’s have our own quiet time. Hold your poppy and sit very still. I will count to eleven, slowly, on my fingers.”* Count silently, finger by finger. Then, softly: *“That’s why we remember them.”*
steps.purpose: Keep a short quiet time together, as people do at 11 o’clock.
students: Count to eleven in your head.
